added_lemmas.statement:
For every admissible radius triple \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\), the oracle threshold and explicit envelope satisfy
\[
U_n(\lambda_n^\star)\leq C_{\mathrm{opt}}\rho_n.
\]
The inequality is deterministic and includes every cap-binding case.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put
\[
b_o=n^{-1/(\kappa+1)},\qquad
b_e=r_{en}^{2/(\kappa+2)},\qquad
b_g=(nr_{1n}^2)^{-1},
\]
with \(b_g=+\infty\) when \(r_{1n}=0\), and let \(L\) be the active maximum in \texttt{def:oracle-threshold}.  Write
\[
S_o=r_{1n}n^{-\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]},\qquad
S_e=r_{1n}r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)},\qquad
S_0=r_{0n}r_{en}.
\]
By \texttt{def:sharp-rate},
\[
\rho_n=Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n})+S_o+S_e+S_0. \tag{1}
\]

First suppose \(L<\lambda_0\), so \(\lambda_n^\star=L\).  Since \(L\geq b_o\),
\[
\frac{r_{1n}}{\sqrt{nL}}\leq r_{1n}L^{\kappa/2}. \tag{2}
\]
Since \(L\geq b_e\), with both conclusions trivial if \(r_{en}=0\),
\[
\frac{r_{en}}{\sqrt nL^{3/2}}
\leq\frac{L^{(\kappa-1)/2}}{\sqrt n}
\leq Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n}),\qquad
\frac{r_{1n}r_{en}}L\leq S_e. \tag{3}
\]
For \(0<\kappa<1\), the second inequality in the first part of (3) follows from \(L\geq b_g\):
\[
n^{-1/2}L^{-(1-\kappa)/2}
\leq n^{-\kappa/2}r_{1n}^{1-\kappa}.
\]
For \(\kappa\geq1\), it follows from \(L<\lambda_0<1\) and the parametric term in \(Q_\kappa\).  The same comparison with \(b_g\) gives
\[
\frac{v_\kappa(L)}{\sqrt n}\leq Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n}) \tag{4}
\]
for \(0<\kappa\leq1\): at \(\kappa=1\),
\(\log(\lambda_0/L)\leq\log_+(nr_{1n}^2)\).  For \(\kappa>1\), (4) is equality.  Finally, taking the positive \(\kappa/2\)-power of the active maximum and bounding the maximum by the sum gives
\[
r_{1n}L^{\kappa/2}
\leq S_o+S_e+Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n}). \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, the \(b_g\) contribution is
\(n^{-\kappa/2}r_{1n}^{1-\kappa}\) for \(0<\kappa<1\) and \(n^{-1/2}\) for \(\kappa=1\); \(b_g\) is inactive for \(\kappa>1\).  Substitution of (2)--(5) into the six terms of \(U_n\) yields
\[
U_n(L)\leq4Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n})+2S_o+3S_e+S_0
\leq4\rho_n. \tag{6}
\]

Now suppose \(L\geq\lambda_0\), so \(\lambda_n^\star=\lambda_0\).  At least one active component is at least \(\lambda_0\).  If \(b_o\geq\lambda_0\), then \(r_{1n}\lambda_0^{\kappa/2}\leq S_o\).  If \(b_e\geq\lambda_0\), then \(r_{1n}\lambda_0^{\kappa/2}\leq S_e\).  In either case, \(Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n})\geq n^{-1/2}\), the radius caps, and
\[
\frac{r_{1n}r_{en}}{\lambda_0}
\leq\lambda_0^{-1}\bar r^{2/(\kappa+2)}S_e
\]
give, term by term,
\[
U_n(\lambda_0)\leq C_{\mathrm{oe}}\rho_n. \tag{7}
\]
If \(0<\kappa\leq1\) and \(b_g\geq\lambda_0\), then
\(r_{1n}\leq(n\lambda_0)^{-1/2}\), also when \(r_{1n}=0\).  Hence
\[
\frac{r_{1n}}{\sqrt{n\lambda_0}}\leq\lambda_0^{-1}n^{-1/2},\quad
r_{1n}\lambda_0^{\kappa/2}\leq
\lambda_0^{-(1-\kappa)/2}n^{-1/2},\quad
\frac{r_{1n}r_{en}}{\lambda_0}\leq
\bar r\lambda_0^{-3/2}n^{-1/2}.
\]
Together with
\(v_\kappa(\lambda_0)n^{-1/2}\),
\(r_{en}n^{-1/2}\lambda_0^{-3/2}\), and \(S_0\), the displayed definition of \(C_{\mathrm g}\) gives
\[
U_n(\lambda_0)\leq C_{\mathrm g}\rho_n. \tag{8}
\]
The cases (7)--(8) exhaust the active maximum.  By the piecewise definition
\(C_{\mathrm{opt}}=4+C_{\mathrm{oe}}+C_{\mathrm g}\) for \(0<\kappa\leq1\) and \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}=4+C_{\mathrm{oe}}\) for \(\kappa>1\), equations (6)--(8) prove the claim.

proposed.justification: It supplies one feasible procedure attaining all four upper-rate components on the broader uniform one-sided-shell class, with a fully explicit finite-threshold constant and without either reservoir-richness condition.
proposed.gap: Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics proves a sufficient studentized limit, and MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap gives asymptotic inference for a bias-corrected trimmed ATE procedure preserving the original target; neither establishes this finite-risk public-function upper frontier or its maximal uniform-shell scope.
proposed.consumer: Analysts with certified black-box prediction errors obtain a clipping rule and an evaluable risk constant for the original population ATE throughout the broader shell class.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The root-MSE block step must depend directly on both the all-N bound and its declared oracle-envelope comparison.

proposed.justification: It closes the exact global-prediction price of one-sided weak overlap across three operational loss criteria, with every median block controlled by the exported finite-threshold inequality.
proposed.gap: The closest published benchmarks concern different estimator-bounded or uniformly overlapped source classes.  Neither they nor weak-overlap limit results supply this four-channel full-ATE minimax frontier.
proposed.consumer: Method developers can use the theorem as the oracle benchmark for clipping, robustification, and higher-order corrections, with the blockwise constant now explicit.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Coverage must use the exported all-N block inequality and the corrected interval definition with its closed-form multiplier.

proposed.justification: The explicit interval upper bound holds on the broader uniform-shell class, while the matching honest expected-length converse remains on the reservoir-rich subclass.
proposed.gap: Existing limited-overlap interval results do not provide this global-L2 bias radius, a closed-form oracle calibration, and a matching reservoir-rich honest-length converse.
proposed.consumer: Applied work can evaluate the displayed confidence radius from the supplied certificates and fixed constants, reading minimax length optimality only under the two richness conditions.

prose_updates.tldr: For fixed one-sided dyadic-shell constants satisfying both \(\texttt{ass:lower-shell-richness}\) and \(\texttt{ass:upper-shell-richness}\), the absolute-risk, root-MSE, fixed-probability for each fixed \(\delta\in(0,\delta_0]\), and honest expected-length for each fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\) frontiers all equal the four-channel rate \(\rho_n\) up to constants.  The clipped estimator, five-block median, and interval upper bounds hold on the broader uniform one-sided-shell class with those two richness conditions deleted.  An exported all-\(N\) inequality gives \(E_P|\widehat\tau_{\lambda,N}-\tau(P)|\leq C_{\mathrm{FT}}U_N(\lambda)\), the explicit oracle comparison gives \(U_n(\lambda_n^\star)\leq C_{\mathrm{opt}}\rho_n\), and \(C_\star=C_{\mathrm{FT}}C_{\mathrm{opt}}\) yields the computable interval multiplier \(K_\alpha=C_\star\max\{\sqrt{10}(10/\alpha)^{1/3},\alpha^{-1}\}\).  Adaptation to unknown shell and nuisance certificates remains open.

project_justification.gap: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR supplies WATE lower-bound templates in its estimator-bounded source class, whereas BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE supplies a lower-rate statement for one mean functional in a different uniformly overlapped structure-agnostic source class.  Neither published class is nested with the present dyadic-shell public-function experiment, so neither citation supports class inclusion or a transferred minimax theorem.  Weak-overlap papers give trimming rules, irregular limits, or sufficient Wald conditions rather than this finite-sample four-risk frontier with an evaluable honest interval.
project_justification.niche: The public-function model isolates the statistical price of knowing only global prediction-error guarantees when treated observations vanish at a boundary.  Its all-\(N\), all-threshold bound keeps the public certificates indexed by the original experiment, so the same inequality controls the full sample and every median block.  Upper estimation and coverage require only the uniform one-sided-shell law; the matching converse requires both explicit reservoir-richness inequalities.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the clipped estimator, five-block median, and a bias-aware interval with the closed-form constants \(C_{\mathrm{FT}}\), \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}\), \(C_\star\), and \(K_\alpha\).  On the broader shell class these objects attain the four-channel upper rate.  On the reservoir-rich subclass, the established signal-only four-channel construction supplies matching absolute-risk, root-MSE, fixed-probability, and honest expected-length lower bounds.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The theorem concerns supplied public functions, bounded certified radii, fixed shell constants, and \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\leq M\); it imposes no pointwise potential-outcome envelope and makes no Wald or Gaussian-limit claim.  The confidence interval is bias-aware and is evaluable when the oracle certificates and fixed class constants are supplied: its multiplier is the displayed algebraic \(K_\alpha\).  The upper interval needs no reservoir richness, whereas matching length optimality uses both richness assumptions.  Adaptation to unknown shell constants, tail exponent, and nuisance radii, bounded-outcome variants, shell constants outside the richness regime, and exact studentized validity remain open.

statement_notes.justification: The exported finite-threshold lemma proves a uniform all-block inequality with explicit \(C_{\mathrm{FT}}\), and the theorem's cap analysis supplies explicit \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}\), so \(C_\star\) is a computable upper-risk witness on the broader shell class.
statement_notes.gap: Existing weak-overlap asymptotic results do not provide this finite-risk public-function envelope with one constant valid for every averaging size and threshold.
statement_notes.consumer: The full-sample estimator, five-block median, and confidence interval can now use the same declared and evaluable constant chain.

statement_notes.justification: Each block has size at least \(n/10\), so the declared all-\(N\) inequality yields mean absolute error at most \(\sqrt{10}C_\star\rho_n\); median amplification then closes the root-MSE upper bound against the established four-channel converse.
statement_notes.gap: The repaired proof no longer relies on a finite-threshold inequality hidden inside another theorem's proof.
statement_notes.consumer: The theorem provides an auditable oracle benchmark for all three estimation loss criteria.

statement_notes.justification: The explicit multiplier \(K_\alpha=C_\star\max\{\sqrt{10}(10/\alpha)^{1/3},\alpha^{-1}\}\) covers both the five-block tail and the \(n<5\) Markov fallback on the broader shell class.
statement_notes.gap: Prior calibration was existential; the corrected procedure is directly evaluable from declared inputs.
statement_notes.consumer: Applied users can compute the bias-aware radius, while the matching expected-length claim remains explicitly limited to the reservoir-rich class.
